items.title: Live: Trump likely target of shooting at correspondents' dinner, top US official says
items.description: US Acting Attorney-General Todd Blanche says the shooter apprehended at the White House correspondents' dinner was likely targeting Donald Trump. Follow live.

items.title: Trump was being shown a party trick. Then gunshots rang out
items.description: Thousands of influential players in Washington filed into a ballroom with the US president. Then shots rang out.

items.title: Trump says shooter's 'manifesto' shows he is a 'sick guy'
items.description: Several US media outlets are reporting on the existence of the manifesto, which reportedly states the shooter wanted to target administration officials and was sent to the suspect's family members just before the attack.

items.title: Trump was 'all set to really rip', but shooting has changed tune on media
items.description: While the latest act of violence wasn't as close as Trump's brush with death in Butler, Pennsylvania, almost two years ago, it will no doubt revive some trauma for Trump and those closest to him.

items.title: 'Membership to nothing': The multi-million-dollar Wild West of rewards clubs
items.description: "Rewards clubs" have exploded in Australia, claiming to have given away hundreds of millions in prizes, but they operate with almost no legal scrutiny.

items.title: An oil shock, a federal budget and the recession we may have to have
items.description: Accompanying the oil shock unfolding in the Strait of Hormuz is a profound change in the way fiscal and monetary policymakers operate. And as the government prepares the budget, with the impact of the Iran war still unfolding, a recession may be ahead.

items.title: Trump turmoil is political kryptonite in Australia
items.description: As Donald Trump's approval in Australia sinks, Anthony Albanese needs to walk a careful line: keep voters convinced of the merits of the alliance, while avoiding the impression he is being too reverential.

items.title: A fascinating admission reveals truth beneath the chest beating in this war
items.description: It's a ceasefire in name only between Israel and its targets in Lebanon, as the wait continues for more talks between the US and Iran.

items.title: The Istanbul hideout: Secret files expose Australia's underworld empire offshore
items.description: Istanbul was once the hideout of choice for Australian crooks. Now a Sydney gangster's legal challenge has revealed how it all unravelled for the "Aussie Cartel".

items.title: More families are sleeping in cars. But they're not the highest housing priority
items.description: An analysis of 12 months of urgent housing and homelessness attendances in Tasmania has shown an alarming spike in people with dependent children needing help — while overcrowding is an increasing concern.

items.title: Australia to sell fleet of Bushmaster armoured vehicles to the Dutch
items.description: Australian Bushmaster armoured vehicles are being sent to the Netherlands following a request to Australia by the Dutch government.

items.title: China's 'quirky' fix for property crisis rewards marathon runners
items.description: Local governments in China are offering marathon runners, AI experts and tennis players subsidies to purchase unwanted properties amid a lingering real estate downturn.

items.title: US allies turning to Japan for defence supplies as Iran War drags on
items.description: Australia's multi-billion-dollar deal with Japan for its future warships could set a template that will help Tokyo rapidly expand defence exports across Asia.

items.title: 'Angry nihilism': Why man behind 'Aussie' posters is bringing them back
items.description: Peter Drew has been hanging 'Aussie' posters in cities around Australia for 10 years, and has no plans to stop.

items.title: Why the bedroom is an 'invisible workplace' for women
items.description: There are biological and psychological reasons behind why women experience more disrupted sleep than men, but experts say the mental load is another powerful yet less obvious contributor.

items.title: Quiz: Have you got the memory to beat our history quiz?
items.description: Which Australian city played host to Expo 88? And what age did the world's oldest spider reach?

items.title: How friendship with Russell Crowe led to an MMA fight
items.description: Bosch & Rockit filmmaker Tyler Atkins's latest feature put his stars through the wringer on camera, but held them with love behind the scenes.

items.title: Two-hour barrier smashed twice in history-making London Marathon
items.description: Kenya's Sabastian Sawe has become the first man to run a marathon in under two hours, winning the London Marathon with a time of 1:59:30.

items.title: Live: Wall Street rallies to record high, ASX set for flat opening
items.description: The S&P 500 rallied to yet another record close as first-quarter earnings continued to beat expectations, but the ASX is priced for a muted opening. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Law breaking drivers to be targeted amid horror year on Queensland roads
items.description: The ABC last year revealed a sharp drop in road safety enforcement hours from police in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic.

items.title: AI ball-tracking technology trialled in Darwin grade cricket
items.description: Darwin's premier women's cricket league has become the first Australian grade competition to use an artificial intelligence umpire review system.

items.title: Government to fund security upgrades for family violence victim-survivors
items.description: Almost 1,700 women facing the danger of family violence will be able to upgrade their home security under a $3.5 million pledge by the Victorian government.

items.title: Sixteen dead in strikes as Ukraine marks 40 years since Chernobyl
items.description: Marking the anniversary, Volodymyr Zelenskyy warns that Russia is using "nuclear terrorism" as a weapon of war.

items.title: How beer and AI are changing the course of Canberra's economic future
items.description: The capital has long been known as a public service town, but with about two in three workers now employed in the private sector and the population expected to reach nearly 700,000 by 2050, is that reputation — and key economic driver — likely to change?

items.title: South-east Qld warned to brace for rainy week amid 'persistent' weather system
items.description: The "very slow-moving" high-pressure system causing the wet weather should "finally get a move on" early next week, the BOM says.
